content_list.content_text: During the first decade of the 21st century, we saw British cinema scoop up a series of awards and director Danny Boyle (b. 1956) venture into Bollywood territory: Slumdog Millionaire (2008) made headlines by winning eight Oscars, including Best Picture.

information.contentText: Due to constraints in the shooting schedule, with the production having only two full days to shoot all the necessary scenes of the war front on the beach at Dunkirk, and a lack of budget to pay for the more than 1,000 extras needed to film those scenes, Joe Wright and cinematographer Seamus McGarvey were forced to condense the shots into a single five-and-a-half-minute take following James McAvoy's character as he moved four hundred meters along the beach. It ended up being one of the most famous scenes in the film.

content_list.content_text: Acclaimed director Mike Leigh (b. 1943) found success with Vera Drake (2004), the story of a woman who performs illegal abortions, while newcomer Stephen Daldry (b. 1961) burst onto the scene with Billy Elliot (2000), his upbeat drama about a boy from a mining community who learns to dance. The film was acclaimed by critics worldwide and caught Hollywood's attention.

British society and its customs were captured both through the lens of Pawel Pawlikowski (b. 1957) in My Summer of Love (2004), which tells the bittersweet story of a teenage romance, and - albeit from a very different angle - by the French co-production directed by Stephen Frears (b. 1941), The Queen (2006), about the death of Princess Diana.

information.contentText: It is an adaptation of the book Q & A by Indian author and diplomat Vikas Swarup. Shot in India, the film tells the story of Jamal Malik Othman, a young man from the slums of Juhu, Mumbai, who appears on the Indian version of the show Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, exceeding everyone's expectations and arousing the suspicion of the host and the police.

content_list.content_text: Independent production companies such as Working Title Films built on the successful comedies and period dramas of the 1990s to secure distribution deals with American studios and produce more films of the kind, such as Bridget Jones's Diary (2001), Love Actually (2003), Pride & Prejudice (2005), and Atonement (2007).

quote.quote: The film combines a Western narrative and an Indian soul in a story deserving of every award.
quote.author: Karen Krizanowich on Slumdog Millionaire

content_list.content_text: Although produced with American money, the Harry Potter franchise (2001-2011) was filmed in the United Kingdom at Leavesden Film Studios, located in Hertfordshire. Its films star local actors and count Englishmen Mike Newell (b. 1942) and David Yates (b. 1963) among their directors. The epic story of the young wizard is one of the highest-grossing film series of all time.

information.contentTitle: Scenes from Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit
information.contentText: Because of their popularity, the characters are considered international icons of modern British culture and of the British people themselves. BBC News has called them "some of the best-known and best-loved stars to come out of the UK". The English website Icons stated that they have done "more to improve the image of the English worldwide than any officially appointed ambassador". The shorts The Wrong Trousers (1993) and A Close Shave (1995) won the Oscar for Best Animated Short Film, and the feature The Curse of the Were-Rabbit (2005) won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.

content_list.content_text: Of all the award winners of this new millennium, the most idiosyncratic was the claymation Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit (2005), by Nick Park (b. 1958) and Steve Box (b. 1967). Produced by Bristol-based Aardman Features and DreamWorks Animation, this inventive and hilarious film, packed with gadgets from the absent-minded inventor Wallace, slapstick humor, and comic references to the world of cinema, delights adults and children alike.

A British film that covered more familiar territory, The Constant Gardener (2005), won numerous awards thanks to the powerful performances of its cast. It stars Ralph Fiennes as the disillusioned British diplomat Justin Quayle, who sets out to uncover the truth behind the murder of his idealistic wife (Rachel Weisz), a human rights activist, after she stumbles upon the shady practices of a major pharmaceutical company in Kenya. Although the plot is complex, Brazilian director Fernando Meirelles (b. 1955) does an excellent job with the exposition without slowing the pace of the narrative.

information.contentText: The film features a predominantly British cast, many of whom had worked with Curtis on previous film and television projects. Shot mainly in London, the screenplay explores different aspects of love, showing ten stories involving ten people who are interconnected in some way.

content_list.content_text: While the revival of British cinema in the 1990s revolved around period dramas and romantic comedies, the 2000s brought weightier films and a United Kingdom willing to reflect on its not-so-distant colonial past in The Last King of Scotland (2006), directed by Scotsman Kevin Macdonald (b. 1967). This low-budget picture became a box office hit thanks to a screenplay co-written by Peter Morgan, co-writer of The Queen, and to a forceful performance by Forest Whitaker (b. 1961) as the Ugandan dictator General Idi Amin, which earned him an Oscar. The mesmerizing Whitaker manages to project the intimidating, murderous nature of this deranged leader in such a way that he comes across as a deeply flawed human being rather than a stereotypical figure of evil.

movies.overview: Jamal Malik is an impoverished Indian teen who becomes a contestant on the Hindi version of ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?’ but, after he wins, he is suspected of cheating.
movies.title: Slumdog Millionaire

movies.overview: As a 13-year-old, fledgling writer Briony Tallis irrevocably changes the course of several lives when she accuses her older sister's lover of a crime he did not commit.
movies.title: Atonement

movies.overview: A story of love and life among the landed English gentry during the Georgian era. Mr. Bennet is a gentleman living in Hertfordshire with his overbearing wife and five daughters, but if he dies their house will be inherited by a distant cousin whom they have never met, so the family's future happiness and security is dependent on the daughters making good marriages.
movies.title: Pride & Prejudice

movies.overview: Cheese-loving eccentric Wallace and his cunning canine pal, Gromit, investigate a mystery in Nick Park's animated adventure, in which the lovable inventor and his intrepid pup run a business ridding the town of garden pests. Using only humane methods that turn their home into a halfway house for evicted vermin, the pair stumble upon a mystery involving a voracious vegetarian monster that threatens to ruin the annual veggie-growing contest.
movies.original_title: Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit
movies.title: Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit

movies.overview: In the Yorkshire countryside, working-class tomboy Mona meets the exotic, pampered Tasmin. Over the summer season, the two young women discover they have much to teach one another, and much to explore together.
movies.title: My Summer of Love

movies.overview: Justin Quayle is a low-level British diplomat who has always gone about his work very quietly, not causing any problems. But after his radical wife Tessa is killed he becomes determined to find out why, thrusting himself into the middle of a very dangerous conspiracy.
movies.title: The Constant Gardener

movies.overview: The Queen is an intimate behind the scenes glimpse at the interaction between HM Elizabeth II and Prime Minister Tony Blair during their struggle, following the death of Diana, to reach a compromise between what was a private tragedy for the Royal family and the public's demand for an overt display of mourning.
movies.title: The Queen

movies.overview: Follows seemingly unrelated people as their lives begin to intertwine while they fall in – and out – of love. Affections languish and develop as Christmas draws near.
movies.title: Love Actually

movies.overview: Young Scottish doctor, Nicholas Garrigan decides it's time for an adventure after he finishes his formal education, so he decides to try his luck in Uganda, and arrives during the downfall of President Obote. General Idi Amin comes to power and asks Garrigan to become his personal doctor.
movies.title: The Last King of Scotland

movies.overview: Shaun lives a supremely uneventful life, which revolves around his girlfriend, his mother, and, above all, his local pub. This gentle routine is threatened when the dead return to life and make strenuous attempts to snack on ordinary Londoners.
movies.title: Shaun of the Dead

movies.overview: Illegal boxing promoter Turkish convinces gangster Brick Top to offer bets on bare-knuckle boxer Mickey at his bookie business. When Mickey does not throw his first fight as agreed, an infuriated Brick Top demands another match. Meanwhile, gangster Frankie Four Fingers comes to place a bet for a friend with Brick Top's bookies, as multiple criminals converge on a stolen diamond that Frankie has come to London to sell.
movies.title: Snatch

movies.overview: A lowly pencil pusher working for MI7, Johnny English is suddenly promoted to super spy after Agent One is assassinated and every other agent is blown up at his funeral. When a billionaire entrepreneur sponsors the exhibition of the Crown Jewels—and the valuable gems disappear on the opening night and on English's watch—the newly-designated agent must jump into action to find the thief and recover the missing gems.
movies.title: Johnny English

CGI reaches a new level with The Matrix, and Latin American and European cinemas capture the world's attention. Click here to see a chronological view of the main events in cinema from 1990 to 2009.
